doc: a data-movement kernel: transpose / permute / concat / slice copy of numel elements.
name: layout
params: {"kind": "str: transpose | concat | copy", "numel": "int"}

doc: max / avg pooling, any window, stride, padding; adaptive pooling as its window.
name: pool2d
params: {"channels": "int", "h": "int", "k": "int", "kind": "str: max | avg", "padding": "int", "stride": "int", "w": "int"}

doc: out[m, n] = a[m, k] @ w[k, n] + b[n] where a, w and b are all activations (no constant operand); k is reduced in 128-element chunks with one accumulator, n is looped over inside the kernel
name: fused_linear_act
params: {"k": "reduction dim", "m": "rows of a (tokens)", "n": "output columns"}
tensors: a [m, k] activation in the row layout (128-element rows, k padded to 128); w [k, n] activation in the row layout (k and n padded to 128); b [n] activation broadcast per output column; out [m, n] activation in the row layout

doc: per-row normalisation over `channels` for `rows` rows: layernorm (mean, var, eps, gamma, beta) | rmsnorm (mean of squares, eps, gamma) | groupnorm handled as rows of a group.
name: row_norm
params: {"channels": "int", "kind": "str: layernorm | rmsnorm", "rows": "int"}
tensors: inputs x [rows, channels], gamma [channels], beta [channels] (layernorm); output y

doc: softmax over n along each of `rows` rows.
name: row_softmax
params: {"n": "int", "rows": "int"}
tensors: input x [rows, n]; output y [rows, n]

doc: sum / mean / max over each row.
name: reduce_rows
params: {"kind": "str: sum | mean | max", "n": "int", "rows": "int"}

doc: y = a (op) b elementwise; broadcast: none (same shape) | row (b is one row of `inner` values repeated over the rows: a bias) | col (b holds `inner` values, one per row of a, each repeated along its row: a per-channel NCHW scale) | scalar.
name: binary
params: {"broadcast": "str: none | row | col | scalar", "inner": "int: length of b's row", "numel": "int", "op": "str: add | sub | mul | div | max | min"}
tensors: inputs a [numel], b [numel] (none) / [inner] (row, col) / [1] (scalar); output y [numel]

doc: y = a * s elementwise, s a compile-time scalar.
name: binary_mul_scalar
params: {"broadcast": "scalar", "inner": 1, "numel": "number of elements", "op": "mul"}
tensors: input a [numel] and output y [numel] in the row layout; scalar is an immediate, not a tensor

doc: y = conv(x, W) + bias for a kh x kw window (stride, padding, groups; groups = cin: depthwise). The kernel walks each output pixel's window itself by row address (one row per input pixel), so no im2col or padding is ever built by the host: out-of-image taps are skipped or read as zero rows. Dense: per tap, a [pixels, cin] x [cin, cout] product accumulated over the taps; depthwise: per tap, a lane-wise multiply of a pixel row by the tap's weight row.
name: conv2d
params: {"bias": "bool", "cin": "input channels", "cout": "output channels", "groups": "int", "h": "input height", "kh": "window height", "kw": "window width", "padding": "int", "stride": "int", "w": "input width"}
tensors: activations x [h * w, cin] in, y [out_h * out_w, cout] out, pixels in row-major (y, x) order, both in the row layout; constants: weights [cout, cin / groups, kh, kw] and bias [cout], laid out offline as the program wants

doc: y = fn(x) elementwise over numel elements (tiled), fn one of the activations.
name: unary
params: {"fn": "str: silu | gelu | gelu_tanh | quick_gelu | sigmoid | tanh | relu | relu6 | hardswish | hardsigmoid | exp | rsqrt | neg | cos | sin | erf", "numel": "int"}
tensors: input x [rows, 128] (numel = rows * 128 rounded up; pad lanes are zero); output y, same shape

doc: y = log(x) elementwise over numel elements, tiled over rows of 128; pad lanes are zero. This is a new `fn` option (`log`) of the existing `unary` primitive, not a new primitive type.
name: unary_log
params: {"fn": "\"log\"", "numel": "int: number of elements, tiled over rows of 128 (numel = rows * 128 rounded up; pad lanes are zero)"}
tensors: input x [rows, 128] in the row layout (pad lanes are zero); output y [rows, 128], same shape, read as direct by the next kernel

doc: y = nearest-neighbor upsample of [channels, h, w] to out_elements outputs; for each output element (oy, ox) it reads the input element (oy // scale, ox // scale) at a compile-time-known index, writing the output in the row layout the next kernel reads.
name: upsample_nearest
params: {"channels": "int: input channels", "h": "int: input height", "mode": "str: nearest2d", "out_elements": "int: number of output elements", "w": "int: input width"}
tensors: input x [channels * h * w] activation in the row layout (128-element rows) as stored by the producing kernel; output y [out_elements] activation in the row layout (128-element rows), read as direct by the next kernel

doc: y = x ** p elementwise over numel elements, with p a compile-time immediate; each exponent gets its own kernel: p=2 is a lane-wise x*x (exact), p=0.5 is sqrt computed as rsqrt(x) then reciprocal (x >= 0 guaranteed here since x is a sum of squares); pad lanes stay zero
name: unary_pow
params: {"fn": "\"pow\"", "numel": "int: number of elements, tiled over rows of 128 (numel = rows * 128 rounded up; pad lanes are zero)", "p": "float: the exponent, a compile-time constant baked into the kernel"}
tensors: input x [rows, 128] in the row layout (pad lanes zero); output y [rows, 128], same shape, read as direct by the next kernel

doc: y[b, i, j] = sum_l a[b, i, l] * b[b, l, j]: a batched matrix product of two activation tensors, accumulated in one accumulator per output element
name: bmm
params: {"batch": "int: number of matrices", "k": "int: shared reduction dim", "m": "int: rows of a", "n": "int: columns of b"}
tensors: a [batch, m, k] and b [batch, k, n] activations in the row layout (each matrix's rows are consecutive 128-lane rows, k and n padded to 128); output y [batch, m, n] in the row layout

doc: y[b,m,n] = a[b,m,k] @ c[b,k,n]: a batched matmul where both operands are activations (no constant weight); one kernel run per batch item b, host loops over b; k is reduced in 128-element chunks inside the kernel with one accumulator and n is looped over inside the kernel, like gemm.
name: bmm_gemm
params: {"k": "reduction", "m": "rows of a (tokens)", "n": "outputs"}
tensors: activations a [m, k] in, c [k, n] in, y [m, n] out, all in the row layout (128-element rows); a and c are read as stored by the producing kernel, y is stored in the row layout for the next kernel

doc: y[i] = sum_{j<=i} x[j]: a cumulative sum along a row of numel elements, computed as a lower-triangular matrix-vector product: the input row is broadcast against a constant lower-triangular mask (1 where j<=i, else 0) and reduced per output position.
name: cumsum_row
params: {"numel": "int: number of elements to cumsum (one row)", "out": "int: number of output elements (one per row)"}
tensors: input x [out, numel] activation in the row layout (each output row i is the input row broadcast, read as stored by the producing kernel); mask [out, numel] constant (lower-triangular 0/1, laid out offline); output y [out] in the row layout (one element per output position, padded to a full 128-lane row), read as direct by the next kernel

doc: y[m, n] = act(x[m, k] @ W[n, k]^T + bias[n]). Any m, k, n: k is reduced in 128-element chunks inside the kernel (one accumulator), n is looped over inside the kernel. Linear, batched matmul, attention and 1x1 convolution (pixels as tokens) lower to it.
name: gemm
params: {"act": "str: none | relu | silu | gelu_tanh (fused at the store)", "bias": "bool: add bias[n]", "k": "reduction", "m": "rows of x (tokens)", "n": "outputs"}
tensors: activations x [m, k] in, y [m, n] out, both in the row layout (so y is the next gemm's x); constants w [n, k] and bias [n], laid out offline as the program wants

doc: y[r] = min over each row of x, computed as a per-row reduction over 128-lane rows (like sum/mean/max); chained with a second call over the row of per-row minima to produce the global amin
name: reduce_rows_min
params: {"kind": "str: min", "n": "int", "rows": "int"}
tensors: input x [rows, n] in the row layout (n padded to 128); output y [rows] in the row layout (one element per row, padded to a full 128-lane row)

doc: y[t, :] = table[idx[t], :] for a constant table and an activation idx: iterates the table rows one by one (loop trip counts come from CRs/LRs, not data); for row r it broadcasts idx[t] as a column and computes a lane-wise match of r against idx[t] (1 where equal, 0 otherwise), producing a one-hot selector that is multiplied by the table row and accumulated over t.
name: one_row_gather
params: {"count": "int: rows gathered (tokens)", "dim": "int: row width", "rows": "int: table rows"}
tensors: table [rows, dim] in the row layout (128-element rows, dim padded to 128); idx [count] activation in the row layout; output y [count, dim] in the row layout, read as direct by the next kernel

doc: y[t, :] = table[idx[t], :]: embeddings, index_select, KV-cache reads.
name: gather_rows
params: {"count": "int: rows gathered", "dim": "int", "rows": "int: table rows"}
tensors: inputs table [rows, dim], idx [count] (row numbers); output y [count, dim]

doc: y[t] = argmax over n elements of each row t of x; the winning index is emitted as a value (one element per row, padded to a full 128-lane row), not used as an address, so the next kernel reads it as data
name: row_argmax
params: {"n": "int: elements per row (padded to 128)", "rows": "int: number of rows"}
tensors: input x [rows, n] in the row layout (n padded to 128); output y [rows] in the row layout (one element per row, padded to a full 128-lane row)
